stories.author: The Lever team
stories.title: What Would An El-Sayed Win Mean For American Zionism?
stories.text: To a certain set of pro-Israel Jewish Democrats, the problem with U.S. Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan isn’t merely that he campaigned with and refuses to fully disavow the far-left streamer Hasan Piker, who they accuse of being antisemitic. It’s also not just that El-Sayed has trafficked, they say, in antisemitic tropes, as when he called Israel “bloodthirsty,” or that he seemed to empathize with a man who attacked a Detroit-area synagogue full of children in March (El-Sayed later said he regretted the comments). And it’s not even that he opposes the existence of Israel as currently constituted and aims to defund all U.S. aid, including for defensive weaponry. All of that is deeply problematic to them. But there’s an even more terrifying prospect for them: That an El-Sayed win in November delivers a decisive blow to the increasingly fragile Zionist movement in America by proving that politicians, even in a hotly contested swing state, no longer must accede to the demands of the pro-Israel electorate in order to win office. “We are entering a world in which candidates are proud to say that they are critical of Israel, where they’re proud to say they’re standing with the P

stories.title: The Speech That Gets You Banned From America
stories.text: Marco Rubio speaking in front of the Acropolis today Fundraising fell off a cliff this summer. Not accepting a dime in corporate ad money allows me to be genuinely independent; but it also means I’m ENTIRELY dependent on readers like you to survive. When I obtained a copy of the internal cable banning those in vaguely “aligned groups” of “far-left terrorists,” I couldn’t help but laugh at the timing. The next day, Rubio was in Greece where, with the Acropolis behind him, he celebrated “free debate and public discussion, the contest of mind with mind.” Rubio even praised Socrates, whom Athens executed on charges of “impiety” and “corrupting the youth.” In the same speech, Rubio leveled basically the same charge, saying that “in too many places, we taught our children to be ashamed of the countries they would inherit.” Under the pretext that certain forms of speech can lead to violence, or even more vaguely, can pose some kind of threat to America’s economy, Rubio has laid out all of the ways that the federal government can decide which ideas are too dangerous and thus can be the basis for denying a visa. stories.author: The Lever team
stories.title: Mike Rogers Invested In Rent Hikes. Now He’s Running For Senate.
stories.text: As corporate landlords made a jackpot off soaring rents, Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers bet on the biggest offender: He made a six-figure investment in a real estate conglomerate as it accelerated evictions and rent hikes. Now, on the campaign trail, the former state representative has proposed an affordable housing strategy described as a “ gimme to homebuilders ” that would create zones where residential developers would pay no federal taxes. In 2023, Blackstone, the world’s largest corporate landlord and private real estate owner, made news for ramping up evictions and raising rents . Not long after that , Rogers invested as much as $250,000 in Blackstone’s private real estate trust — investments he still holds today. After Blackstone purchased five university housing apartments in Rogers’ home state in 2022, the company raised students' rent by 26 percent over the following three years — double the area’s average rent increase. In early 2023, Blackstone started eviction proceedings against hundreds of tenants throughout the U.S. while sunsetting its pandemic-era rent forbearance programs.
